title: Place models and tensors on the correct compute device / Adjust training batch size to fit available memory / Diagnose training memory exhaustion

steps.title: Place models and tensors on the correct compute device

blocks.text: Check availability, then verify placement for the model, features and targets together.

Choose torch.device("cuda") only after checking torch.cuda.is_available(); otherwise use the supported CPU device. Place all participants compatibly: model.to(device) for the model and tensor.to(device) for every input and target tensor. Inspect the model parameters’ device and both minibatch tensor devices, and run a bounded forward/backward fixture to check the declared placement.

Test valid, boundary and failure fixtures with assert predicates. A false predicate raises AssertionError in ordinary non-optimized execution. For an authorized supplied Compute Engine VM, gcloud compute instances start INSTANCE --zone=ZONE and gcloud compute instances stop INSTANCE --zone=ZONE change its lifecycle state; wait for the operation and inspect the resulting state. Connect to the running authorized VM with gcloud compute ssh INSTANCE --zone=ZONE to execute the workload.

before.code:
import torch
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
# A device choice alone does not move the model or tensors.
inspect_devices(model, features, targets)

after.code:
model = model.to(device)
features = features.to(device)
targets = targets.to(device)
assert all(p.device == features.device for p in model.parameters())
assert targets.device == features.device
loss = loss_fn(model(features), targets)
loss.backward()

blocks.change_summary: Move and check all three participants.

steps.title: Place models and tensors on the correct compute device

blocks.text: Use gcloud compute instances describe INSTANCE --zone=ZONE to inspect the instance status and identity before and after the authorized lifecycle action. Stop the authorized instance after the bounded workload with gcloud compute instances stop INSTANCE --zone=ZONE, wait for completion and verify its stopped state.

steps.title: Place models and tensors on the correct compute device

blocks.text: On the supplied VM, inspect its identity and state, start it under the approved scope and connect for the bounded workload. If CUDA is available, select the supported CUDA device; otherwise use the supported CPU path. Move the model, features and targets to the selected device. Inspect parameter and tensor devices and run a bounded forward/backward fixture. Moving features while leaving targets on another device does not meet the placement contract. When the measurement finishes, stop the authorized instance, wait and verify its state.
The device record should identify the actual execution choice rather than merely copying the intended hardware label.

steps.title: Place models and tensors on the correct compute device

steps.title: Check: Verify consistent tensor/model placement on an authorized instance and restore its stopped state.

public.prompt: torch.cuda.is_available() reports False on the supplied supported CPU environment. What selection follows the availability rule?

options.text: Select torch.device("cpu") and record that actual choice.
Select CUDA because the requested workload would be faster there.
Select CUDA because the VM is described informally as GPU-capable.

o2.message: A desired speedup does not establish CUDA availability.

o3.message: Actual measured availability governs the device choice, not an informal label.

correct.message: Correct. Select torch.device("cpu") and record that actual choice.

incorrect.message: Recheck the stated contract. A desired speedup does not establish CUDA availability. Actual measured availability governs the device choice, not an informal label.

hints: Use the measured availability, not the desired hardware.

steps.title: Apply: Verify consistent tensor/model placement on an authorized instance and restore its stopped state.

public.prompt: Inspect a bounded workload on an already authorized supplied Compute Engine VM. INSTANCE and ZONE below refer only to that supplied VM. Judge compatible placement, valid/CPU-boundary/failure assertions and the complete lifecycle record. Sort every excerpt into Supported (all stated contract claims hold) or Defective (at least one stated claim violates the contract). Each excerpt is independent; comments describe recorded fixture evidence.

items.text:
describe INSTANCE --zone=ZONE: identity matches authorization; initial status TERMINATED
start INSTANCE --zone=ZONE: operation completed
describe: same identity, RUNNING
ssh INSTANCE --zone=ZONE: connected
# torch.cuda.is_available() determines device; actual choice recorded.
# model.to(device), features.to(device), targets.to(device) once per needed input.
# Parameter/input/target devices asserted equal; bounded forward/backward
# and prediction complete. Supported CPU boundary passes.
# Deliberate incompatible-device predicate raises AssertionError.
stop INSTANCE --zone=ZONE: operation completed
describe: same identity, TERMINATED
# Commands above use gcloud compute instances, except gcloud compute ssh.

# CUDA is available; model and features are on cuda, targets are on cpu.
# A required computation consumes all three.
# Claim that moving features alone establishes compatible placement.

# Correct compatible devices; bounded workload complete.
gcloud compute instances stop INSTANCE --zone=ZONE
# Do not wait or describe the resulting state; report shutdown verified.

e1.message: The authorized identity and lifecycle states are verified, actual availability guides compatible placement, and bounded execution plus assertion outcomes provide evidence.

e2.message: Targets and model state also need compatible placement; moving features alone is insufficient.

e3.message: Issuing stop is not verification; wait for completion and inspect the resulting authorized instance state.

correct.message: Correct. You distinguished the contract-satisfying evidence from the defective excerpts.

incorrect.message: Recheck each excerpt against its declared contract; successful execution or a plausible shape alone does not establish every acceptance claim.

hints: Inspect all participating tensors and both ends of the authorized lifecycle.

steps.title: Adjust training batch size to fit available memory

blocks.text: Compare measured training peaks and completed work, not just input bytes.

Input bytes alone are not peak training memory. Live tensors and other allocations also count, and larger minibatches ordinarily need more activation storage. Change only DataLoader batch_size in the comparison. Keep observation alignment and the supplied training task unchanged. For a CUDA trial, reset_peak_memory_stats() before the measured workload and inspect torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() afterward to obtain peak allocated tensor bytes.

A reported allocated-tensor peak does not include every component of GPU usage; compare the supplied budget with the memory quantity it actually governs. Among eligible batch sizes, compare completed work per elapsed time. Choose within the measured memory bound. Estimate the matrix-shaped minibatch allocation as batch_rows × feature_columns × bytes_per_feature_element, add the target allocation under its dtype, and compare this estimate with the actual observed peak.

steps.title: Adjust training batch size to fit available memory

blocks.text: In the supplied fixture, a batch has 100 rows, 20 four-byte features and 100 four-byte targets. The feature estimate is 8,000 bytes and the target estimate is 400 bytes. Compare that estimate with the observed training peak rather than calling 8,400 bytes total training memory. For CUDA trials, reset the peak statistic before the bounded workload and inspect peak allocated tensor bytes after it. Vary only the declared DataLoader batch size, keeping alignment and task fixed.

Compare completed work per elapsed time for eligible settings, using the memory quantity the supplied budget actually governs. A setting that fails the memory requirement is not rescued by higher throughput.

incorrect.message: Recheck the stated contract. Higher throughput does not excuse violating the declared memory bound. Input estimates do not replace the measured training-memory quantity governed by this bound.

public.prompt: Inspect otherwise matched CUDA DataLoader trials. The budget governs peak allocated tensor bytes, not reserved or total GPU usage. For the illustrative 100-row, 20-feature, four-byte-feature/four-byte-target batch, input estimates must be reported separately: features 8000, targets 400, combined 8400 bytes. e2.message: Feature and target storage do not define peak training memory.

blocks.text: Locate the failure among simultaneous live allocations before choosing one correction.

Distinguish the CUDA readings: memory_allocated measures tensor-occupied memory, while memory_reserved includes caching-allocator storage. Inspect the workload’s peak allocated and reserved memory and the point of failure before attributing the failure to the input batch alone. Retaining tensors attached to computation graphs can retain graph memory; use detached/scalar diagnostic values when gradients through those saved values are not needed.

empty_cache releases unused cache for other uses, not storage still occupied by live tensors. Change one supported factor, such as reducing minibatch size or removing an unnecessary retained graph reference, and verify completion and the measured peak on the same bounded workload. Account for each parameter, gradient, activation and batch matrix as element_count × element_width, then sum simultaneously live allocations rather than only the input matrix.

left.code:
import torch
allocated = torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
reserved = torch.cuda.memory_reserved()
peak_allocated = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()
peak_reserved = torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved()
# Retaining loss can retain its computation graph.
diagnostic_history.append(loss)
# empty_cache cannot free live tensor storage.

right.code:
# Contrast: retain scalar evidence when its gradient is not needed.
diagnostic_history.append(loss.item())
# For the rerun, remove the unnecessary retained graph reference.
# Change only that supported factor and remeasure the same workload.
parameter_elements = F * H + H
parameter_bytes = parameter_elements * parameter_element_width
live_bytes = sum(element_count * element_width
                 for element_count, element_width in simultaneous_allocations)
verify_completion_and_peak_on_same_workload()

blocks.takeaway: Sum simultaneously live allocations, not only the input matrix.

blocks.text: For a linear layer with input width F and output width H, the weight matrix has F × H elements and its bias has H, supporting the parameter-allocation reference.

For a linear layer with input width 20 and output width 10, the weight reference contains 200 elements and the bias 10. At four bytes each, those parameters alone account for 840 bytes, before gradients, activations and batch matrices are counted. Sum simultaneously live allocations using their own element widths. Inspect peak allocated and reserved evidence and whether saved diagnostics retain computation graphs. Change one supported factor, such as a smaller batch or removing an unnecessary retained graph reference, then rerun the same bounded task and verify completion and peak.
Use scalar or detached diagnostic values where gradients through the saved values are not needed.
Unused cache and live tensors are different. empty_cache cannot release storage still occupied by live tensors.

steps.title: Check: Diagnose a reproduced out-of-memory failure from simultaneous allocations and runtime measurements.

public.prompt: Diagnostics save each loss tensor with its graph even though no future derivative through the saved values is needed. Which isolated change addresses this evidence?

options.text: Call empty_cache while retaining all graph-connected losses and claim live tensors were freed.
Keep the graph-connected losses and relabel reserved memory as unused tensor-free memory.
Save scalar or detached diagnostic values instead, then rerun the same bounded workload and compare measured peaks.

o1.message: empty_cache cannot release storage still occupied by live tensors.

o2.message: Reserved and allocated quantities are distinct; relabeling does not remove live graph references.

correct.message: Correct. Save scalar or detached diagnostic values instead, then rerun the same bounded workload and compare measured peaks.

incorrect.message: Recheck the stated contract. empty_cache cannot release storage still occupied by live tensors. Reserved and allocated quantities are distinct; relabeling does not remove live graph references.

hints: Ask whether the diagnostic really needs a gradient connection.

steps.title: Apply: Diagnose a reproduced out-of-memory failure from simultaneous allocations and runtime measurements.

public.prompt: Review memory-exhaustion evidence for a 20-input, 10-output linear layer with four-byte parameters. Its parameter reference is 840 bytes before gradients, activations and batch matrices. The failed bounded run accumulates graph-connected loss diagnostics not needed for later differentiation. At the reproduced failure point, the supplied simultaneous-live ledger is {'parameters': 840, 'gradients': 840, 'batch_features': 8000, 'batch_targets': 400, 'activations': 4000, 'retained_graphs': 20000} bytes; the allocator rejects a further required allocation under a 20000-byte allocated-tensor bound. Failed allocated/reserved peaks and the point of failure are retained. Sort every excerpt into Supported (all stated contract claims hold) or Defective (at least one stated claim violates the contract). Each excerpt is independent; comments describe recorded fixture evidence.

items.text:
# Sum the supplied simultaneous-live ledger: 34080 bytes.
# Parameter reference is (20*10+10)*4 = 840 bytes.
# Failed peak allocated=34080; reserved=38080 bytes.
# Graph-connected saved diagnostics require no future derivatives.
# Single correction: store loss.item() instead of the graph-connected loss.
# Same bounded task completes; corrected allocated peak=14080,
# corrected reserved peak=18080 bytes.
# Retain both records; corrected allocated peak meets the 20000-byte bound.

# Large live-tensor allocation remains referenced.
torch.cuda.empty_cache()
# Claim: the still-live tensor storage must now be released.

# Linear-layer reference counts only 20 input values: 20*4 bytes.
# Declare this the entire parameter allocation and ignore the bias.

e1.message: The ledger includes parameters, gradients, batch storage, activations and retained graphs at the same instant; removing only unnecessary diagnostic graph retention is supported by completion and the corrected allocated peak.

e2.message: empty_cache releases unused cache, not memory occupied by live tensors.

e3.message: Weight storage depends on input times output width; the bias adds output-width elements. Counting only the input vector is not a parameter reference.

correct.message: Correct. You distinguished the contract-satisfying evidence from the defective excerpts.

incorrect.message: Recheck each excerpt against its declared contract; successful execution or a plausible shape alone does not establish every acceptance claim.

hints: Count simultaneously live objects and distinguish them from unused cache.
